important.name: Plan 2031 TASK-10 live-session confirmation has no receipt
important.summary:
The branch records receipts for TASK-1 to TASK-9 only; TASK-10 (ActionPlan lines 355-377) is still PENDING. It is the item that confirms the host facts the whole design rests on, chief among them (a) that the drawn AssistantMessage text of a reply's last block fingerprints equal to turn.complete's answer, which the spec (Left to the builder) calls 'the one place approach A can fail silently'. If that fact is false, no reply ever gains a stamp and nothing reports it. The plugin README lists the facts as known limitations (plugins/lap-stamp/README.md:130-142), but the plan the PR implements is not complete and its PIP shows TASK-10 open.

Also (overall): Receipts exist for TASK-1 to TASK-9 only. TASK-10 (the developer's `claude --plugin-dir plugins/lap-stamp` session) is the step that confirms the AssistantMessage text normalizes to turn.complete's answer, the delivery door, the bridge/slash-command origin kinds, the TurnDuration props and resume session ids. The README lists them as Known limitations, so this is disclosed, but the spec calls the text match 'the one place approach A can fail silently'.
fix: Run the TASK-10 session (`claude --plugin-dir plugins/lap-stamp`), record any differing fact in DesignEvolution through evolution_api with its fix cited, and record the TASK-10 receipt before merging.
If the developer decides to merge first, close TASK-10 through the plan driver as deferred (an evolution entry naming the deferral) so the plan does not read as complete-but-pending.
Run TASK-10 before merging and record its receipt (and any differing fact as a DesignEvolution entry), or state in the PR description that the merge precedes the live check.

important.name: Laps file append is a whole-file read-modify-write that loses rows from concurrent sessions
important.summary:
completed() reads the entire laps file at the start of the stop (lapsText, line 284), awaits several host calls (read of sessionAtom and clockAtom, update, keepRow), then writes back `withLine(text, rowLine(row))` with $.fs.write (line 292), replacing the file. The laps file is one per checkout (config.ts LAPS_PATH, plan V4), so two Claude Code sessions open in the same checkout share it; the `serial` queue (line 47-52, 'no two writes interleave') only orders work inside one mod instance. When session B appends between session A's read and A's write, A's write drops B's row, and on the ranged path (readRanges, a file that grew after the stat) the bytes past the stat size are truncated the same way. The lost row is never restored: B holds it only in memory until B's process exits, after which its reply loses its stamp on every redraw. The docstring at line 275 calls this an append, which the code does not do.

Also (overall): completed() reads the whole laps file (lapsText, ranged reads above 4 MiB) and writes back text + the new line with $.fs.write (lap.ts:284,292). Spec D5 and the mod README (README.md:71, 'Append-only') promise an append-only file, one per checkout, but two sessions in the same checkout that stop close together each read the same text and the second write drops the first session's row. The serial queue (ctx.tail) only orders hooks inside one process. The cost also grows with the file: every stop rereads the whole file, in 3 MiB ranges once it is over the host's read cap. Nothing in the README's Known limitations states either effect.

Also (runtime): The laps file collects one row per turn of every session in the checkout and nothing prunes it. completed() reads the full file (ranged reads in 3 MiB pieces past 4 MiB, lines 196-220) and rewrites it in full on every main-loop stop, so the cost of each stop grows with all history. The ranged read handles a file past the host's 4 MiB answer cap, but the write of that same text goes through a single $.fs.write; if writes share the cap, every later row stays memory-only (fail-open, but silent).
fix: Re-read the laps file immediately before the write and append the row to that fresh text (and only write when the fresh read succeeded), so the window shrinks to the single read-write pair; state the remaining race in the README Limits.
After the write, re-read and confirm the file still contains the row's line; on a miss, merge and rewrite once more (bounded retry).
Use a host append primitive if the engine offers one ($.fs.append or a write option) instead of rewriting the file.

Before the write, reread the file and only write when its text still equals the text read at the start; on a mismatch rebuild withLine from the new text and retry once (narrows the window; the serial queue already prevents in-process interleaving).

If the host offers no append primitive, state the cross-session race and the per-stop full-file rewrite in plugins/lap-stamp/README.md Known limitations and change 'Append-only' (README.md:71) to say rows are only ever added but the file is rewritten on each stop.
Bound the file: when the text exceeds a threshold, keep only the newest N rows (or the rows of the newest sessions) in the rewrite, and document the bound in the README.
Document the unbounded growth and the write-size limit in the README Limits section if pruning is out of scope for this PR.

important.name: load() does not apply the session-switch rule clockFor() applies: a new session keeps the old session's last prompt
important.summary:
clockFor (lap.ts:95-105) rebuilds lastPromptAt and consumedAt from the new session's own rows when the session id changes, and the test 'a switched session rebuilds the clock from its own rows: no stale since prompt' (lap.test.ts:576) pins that intent. load() (lap.ts:296-308), run on session.start and session.attach, sets sessionAtom to the new id and then calls seedLastPrompt, which takes the max of the clock's existing lastPromptAt and the new session's newest prompt. When session.start or session.attach fires in-process with a different session id, the previous session's lastPromptAt survives; because sessionAtom now equals the new id, completed() takes clockFor's same-session branch and the next wake row records last_prompt_at and since_prompt_ms from another session's prompt, against D4 ('the newest prompt_at of the session'). The comment at lap.ts:91 says /clear and resume raise no session.start, but that is one of the host readings TASK-10 has not yet confirmed; the two paths that handle the same event should not disagree.

Also (runtime): clockFor (lines 89-105) treats a session id change as a switch: lastPromptAt and consumedAt are replaced by the new session's newest press (null when none) and the wake reason clears. load() (lines 296-308), run on session.attach, sets sessionAtom to the current id and then applies seedLastPrompt, which keeps the newer of the old session's lastPromptAt and the new session's. After a /clear (no session.start, per the clockFor docstring) followed by a session.attach before the next stop, sessionAtom already equals the new id, so clockFor takes the same-session branch and the next wake row's since_prompt_ms is measured from the previous session's last prompt.
fix: In load(), read the known session before overwriting sessionAtom and, when it is non-null and differs from the new session, update the clock with clockFor(c, session, known, text) (or the same rebuild: lastPromptAt and consumedAt from newestPromptAt(rows), pendingWake null) instead of seedLastPrompt; keep seedLastPrompt for the same-session and first-session cases. Add a lap.test.ts case: turn in S1, session.start with S2, wake turn: since_prompt is null.
In load(), read sessionAtom first and, when it is non-null and differs from the current session, apply the clockFor switch rule (`clockFor(clock, session, known, text)`) instead of seedLastPrompt.

important.name: Release-notes check is invisible to PR test selection
important.summary:
test_the_release_notes_list_the_mod opens docs/RELEASES/v{version}.md through a path built at runtime from marketplace.json. tools/select_tests.py picks a test only when its source names a changed file's basename or when it walks a declared WALK_ROOTS folder. This test does neither, so a pull request that edits or drops the lap-stamp row in docs/RELEASES/v1.1.0.md skips it, and the break only shows up in the full run on main. CLAUDE.md (Tests) requires a test that reaches a file by a runtime route to spell that file out. test_arc_straps_registration.py already solves the same problem with a glob over docs/RELEASES plus WALK_ROOTS = ("docs/RELEASES/",).

Also (system_shape): test_the_release_notes_list_the_mod reads `metadata.version` from marketplace.json and requires a `| lap-stamp |` row in `docs/RELEASES/v<that version>.md`. That holds only while 1.1.0 is the proposed release. CLAUDE.md (Releases) has the next branch that bumps any plugin create `v<X.Y.Z>.md` and move `metadata.version`. That file gets a row only for plugins that changed, so an unchanged lap-stamp fails this test on a branch that never touched it. The path is also built at runtime (`v{version}.md`) and never written out, so `tools/select_tests.py` does not pick the test when a release-notes file changes. The row check also ignores the version, so a release row that disagrees with plugin.json still passes. The repo already has a working pattern for this: `tests/contract/test_arc_straps_registration.py:13,63-74` walks every `docs/RELEASES/v*.md` under `WALK_ROOTS = ("docs/RELEASES/",)` and requires some row to carry the manifest version.
fix: Follow tests/contract/test_arc_straps_registration.py: add a module-level WALK_ROOTS = ("docs/RELEASES/",) and collect the lap-stamp rows by globbing (repo_root / "docs" / "RELEASES").glob("v*.md"), then assert that one row carries the manifest's version (| lap-stamp | ... | 0.1.0 |).

Rewrite the check the way test_arc_straps_registration.py does it. Declare `WALK_ROOTS = ("docs/RELEASES/",)`, collect every `| lap-stamp |` row across `docs/RELEASES/v*.md`, and assert that one ends in the version from `plugins/lap-stamp/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. The test is a planned (frozen) test, so record the change as a DesignEvolution entry and cite it at record time.

Keep the current-release lookup but assert only the manifest-version row, and spell out the release file name in the source so selection can see it. This still fails once the version rolls, so the first option is preferred.

minor.name: Root README state_dir key row does not list lap-stamp/laps.jsonl

Prefix the line with the PR number once the PR is opened: '- #<N> Feat(lap-stamp): ...'.
Once the PR is opened, change line 127 to start with `- #<N> Feat(lap-stamp): new mod.`

minor.name: prompt.submit hook works before next, against TASK-7's 'every hook awaits next first'; no DesignEvolution entry
minor.summary: The plan's TASK-7 action says every hook awaits next first. The prompt.submit hook (lap.ts:329-339) queues the press before next and takes it back on a drop, for a stated reason (the turn starts inside next). The design is sound and tested (lap.test.ts:495-524), but DesignEvolution.json records only EX1 and EX2, so the plan and the code disagree with no record.
fix: Record an EX3 in docs/plans/2031/DesignEvolution.json through evolution_api: prompt.submit takes the press before next so the turn that starts inside next finds it, and withdraws it when next returns a drop.

minor.name: Manifest and marketplace descriptions differ, and both promise 'time since the last prompt' on every stamp
minor.summary: plugin.json:4 ends 'laps are kept in a JSONL file' and marketplace.json:99 ends 'laps are kept in a git-ignored JSONL file'. Elsewhere in the marketplace the two copies match word for word (for example bubble-stamp), and test_arc_straps_registration.py:77-80 enforces that for arc-straps. Both texts also say the mod stamps 'the clock time, lap and time since the last prompt', but stamp.ts:39-43 adds `since prompt` only on a wake turn with a prompt behind it (spec D6, README lines 15-21).
fix: Use one string in both files, for example: "Times each main-conversation turn from the developer's prompt to its stop and stamps the clock time and lap under the reply (a wake-up adds the time since the last prompt); laps are kept in a git-ignored JSONL file".

minor.name: README calls the laps file append-only; the glue rewrites the whole file
minor.summary: plugins/lap-stamp/README.md:71-72 says 'Append-only, one row ... per turn'. completed() reads the whole file (lapsText, ranged above 4 MiB) and writes back `withLine(text, rowLine(row))` (plugins/lap-stamp/hooks/lap.ts:284,292), and skips the write entirely when the file exists but does not read. The serial queue protects one session, but two sessions in the same checkout each read-then-write, so the later write drops the other's row, and every turn costs a full read and rewrite of a file that is never rotated. The README states neither the single-writer assumption nor the skip.
fix: Reword the laps-file paragraph: each turn reads the file and writes it back with one more line (existing lines kept verbatim), a file that exists but cannot be read is left untouched and the row stays in memory only, and concurrent sessions in one checkout can lose a row.
Switch the write to a host append primitive, if the host API offers one, and keep the README's append-only wording.

minor.name: Mod README hooks table omits the session.append delivery hook
minor.summary:
'Hooks it registers' lists session.start/attach, prompt.submit, turn.start/turn.complete and the two renders, but registerPresses also registers `session.append` filtered to door `delivery` (plugins/lap-stamp/hooks/lap.ts:343-348), the signal that attaches a mid-turn lap press to the running turn (D2, EX2). The table is the README's contract for what register.ts wires, and it misses one hook.

Also (overall): The 'Hooks it registers' table (README.md:115-121) omits the session.append hook on door 'delivery' (lap.ts:343-348), the only path that attaches a mid-turn press to the running turn (D2). The State section (README.md:125-126) says $.state['lap-stamp'] holds 'the session's rows and the pending press'; it holds rows, the whole clock (pending presses, running turn, consumed-press marker, last prompt, pending wake reason) and the session id (types/index.d.ts:74-83).

Also (system_shape): The README says `register.ts` 'wires' the hooks in its table (lines 113-121). The table lists session.start/attach, prompt.submit, turn.start/complete and the two render sites. It leaves out `on('session.append', { door: 'delivery' }, ...)` (plugins/lap-stamp/hooks/lap.ts:343-348). That hook carries D2's mid-turn delivery rule, which the README's own Lap rules section (lines 35-38) relies on. The State section (lines 123-126) says `$.state['lap-stamp']` 'holds the session's rows and the pending press'. types/index.d.ts:74-83 declares three keys: `rows`, `clock` (pending presses, the running turn, the consumed-press marker, the last prompt and the wake reason) and `session` (the current session id, which render filters on).
fix: Add a row: `session.append` (door `delivery`, the main loop) | A lap-press delivery into the running turn attaches that press to it and restarts its lap; a `queue` row is not a delivery.

Add a row '`session.append` (door `delivery`, main loop) | Attaches a lap press delivered into the running turn to that turn (D2).' to the hooks table, and rewrite the State sentence to list rows, clock and session id.

Add a row to the hook table: `session.append` (door `delivery`, main loop) | 'Attaches a lap press delivered into the running turn to that turn (D2); a `queue` row is ignored.' Change the State sentence to name the three keys: `rows` (the session's rows), `clock` (pending presses, the running turn and the prompt markers) and `session` (the current session id).

minor.name: Mod README State section understates the state contract
minor.summary: plugins/lap-stamp/README.md:125-126 says `$.state['lap-stamp']` holds 'the session's rows and the pending press'. The contract in plugins/lap-stamp/types/index.d.ts:74-84 holds `rows`, the whole `clock` (pending presses, running turn, consumed-press marker, last prompt, pending wake reason) and the current `session` id, which render uses to filter rows (render.tsx:36-37).
fix: Reword: holds the session's rows, the lap clock (pending presses, the running turn, the consumed-press marker, the last prompt and the pending wake reason) and the current session id; render reads only rows and session.

minor.name: Wake reason window is 'since the last turn start', not the spec's 'since the previous main-loop stop'
minor.summary: The spec's Builder's calls (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-25-lap-stamp-design.md:140-142) define `wake` as the origin kind of the newest non-lap `prompt.submit` since the previous main-loop stop, else null for 'a post-compaction resume or a continuation with no submission'. In the code, `submitted` (clock.ts:56-59) sets `pendingWake` on every non-lap submission and only `started` (clock.ts:97-108) clears it. So a non-lap submission made while turn N runs (for example a task notification delivered into N) survives N's stop. A following turn N+1 that starts with no submission then records that origin as its `wake` instead of null. The README (line 80) says only 'the newest non-lap submission', so neither document states the window the code uses.
fix: Match the spec: clear `pendingWake` in `stopped` (clock.ts:134-147) so only submissions after the stop count. Add a clock.test.ts case in which a mid-turn task-notification followed by a start with no submission gives `wake: null`.
Keep the start-to-start window as a deliberate choice: record it in DesignEvolution and state the window in the README `wake` field row (line 80).

minor.name: Subagent delivery rows are not covered
minor.summary: afterDelivery returns early for a session.append delivery that carries an agentId (lap.ts:321), but no lap.test case appends a delivery row with an agentId during a running main-loop turn. If that guard regressed, a subagent's delivery would restart the main turn's lap without any test catching it.
fix: Add a case to 'delivery into a running turn (D2)': begin t1, press with turnId t1, append a delivery row with agentId 'agent-1', stop t1, and assert the row is kind wake with lap_ms measured from t1's start.

minor.name: Refused-state test: name says 'during a press' and one assertion cannot fail
minor.summary: world(on, '{}', { state: true }) refuses every lap-stamp state.set for the whole test, not only during a press. The mock returns the deny before it records into seen.state, so expect(seen.state.size).toBe(0) holds whatever the glue does and can never fail. Only expectUntouched carries the behavior under test.
fix: Rename the test to 'a refused state store changes nothing the host returned and throws nothing' and replace the size assertion with one that can fail, e.g. that the turn's row still reaches the laps file (fileRows(seen) has length 1) or that seen.writes is what the glue should produce when the atom is refused.
Or refuse state only around the press (a flag the test flips) and assert that the following turn still records.

minor.name: Raw BOM bytes embedded in a template literal
minor.summary: textOf returns `\uFEFF${body}` by embedding the literal U+FEFF bytes (EF BB BF) inside the template string at lap.ts:125; the character is invisible in editors and diffs, so the line reads as `${body}` and an editor that strips BOMs or normalizes the file silently changes behavior (the BOM round trip that lap.test.ts:703 checks). row.test.ts:151 has the same invisible literal.
fix: Replace the invisible character with an escape: return hasBom ? `\uFEFF${body}` : body (and '\uFEFF' + ... in row.test.ts:151).

minor.name: resolveWatch counts a failed git probe as a sure answer, contradicting its docstring
minor.summary: resolveWatch's docstring (lines 161-164) says absence is sure 'only when every host call answered'. toplevelOf (lines 150-159) swallows a rejected or timed-out $.process.run into '' (and caches that failure for the process lifetime), so resolveWatch cannot tell a failed git call from a real 'not a repository' answer and never clears isSure for it. A git timeout then lets a sure absence deactivate the glue, or lets a linked-worktree session fall through to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and write its laps under the main checkout.
fix: Have toplevelOf report a failed run (rejection or timeout, as opposed to a non-zero exit) to resolveWatch, which calls doubt() for it, and do not cache that failure in ctx.toplevels.
Alternatively narrow the docstring to say a failed git probe counts as an answer and is remembered.

minor.name: 'Either season' host-offset test cannot fail on a UTC runner
minor.summary: The test builds its expected value with the same formula row.ts uses (isoLocal(ms, eastOffsetMin(new Date(ms).getTimezoneOffset()))). On the Ubuntu CI job, where the mod tests run, the zone is UTC, so winter and summer offsets are both +00:00. A regression that applied a single fixed offset (for example the offset of 'now') to every instant would still pass, so the per-instant claim in the name is never exercised there.
fix: Let the host-offset lookup be injected (for example buildRow taking an optional offsetAt(ms) function) and test with a fake that returns different offsets for the two instants.
Or rename the test so it only claims the host offset is applied, and drop the 'either season' wording.

minor.name: rowLine 'keys in column order' checks only the first four keys
minor.summary: The test name promises column order, but the assertion only checks a prefix covering v, session, turn and kind. If the other ten fields were reordered (prompt_at through answer_len), the test would still pass, and the JSON.parse equality ignores key order.
fix: Assert Object.keys(JSON.parse(line)) equals the full ordered list ['v','session','turn','kind','wake','prompt_at','start_at','stop_at','last_prompt_at','lap_ms','since_prompt_ms','reason','answer_hash','answer_len'].

minor.name: newestPromptAt 'prompt_at wins' test never tests prompt_at on its own
minor.summary: In 'the newest prompt_at wins as epoch ms', the late row has both prompt_at and last_prompt_at set to T0 + 5000. newestPromptAt reads both fields, so the test still passes if the prompt_at branch is removed. No other test in the file gives prompt_at a value newer than last_prompt_at, so the claim in the test name has no assertion behind it.
fix: Build the late row with timing { ...promptTiming, promptAt: T0 + 5000, lastPromptAt: T0 }, so only prompt_at carries T0 + 5000, and keep both order assertions.

minor.name: Stamp clock re-derives HH:MM:SS in the render host's zone instead of showing the stored value
minor.summary: stamp.ts's module docstring (lines 4-8) says 'A stamp shows the row's own stored values, never recomputed ones.' clockOf (lines 31-36) parses stop_at into a Date and formats getHours/getMinutes/getSeconds in the zone of the process drawing the stamp, ignoring the offset buildRow stored in the row. A row written under one zone (or a forced offsetMin) and drawn under another shows a different clock than the file holds.
fix: Take HH:MM:SS straight from the stored ISO text (characters 11-19, after the ISO_LOCAL shape check) and keep the placeholder for a string that does not match.
Alternatively reword the docstring and clockOf's doc to say the clock time is converted to the drawing host's zone.

minor.name: ClockState and PluginState field docs disagree with the reducers and glue
minor.summary: types/index.d.ts:68 documents lastPromptAt as the 'Newest press of the session', but clock.ts only raises it for used presses (stopped, foldLostRun, seedLastPrompt; clock.ts:111 says 'newest used press'); a pending press never moves it. types/index.d.ts:66 says consumedAt is the press 'a stopped turn used', but foldLostRun (a lost turn) and seedLastPrompt (the file) also raise it. types/index.d.ts:80 says session is 'null before session.start', but keepRow sets it on the first stop when no session.start ran (the case lap.test.ts covers as 'the turn works without a session.start').
fix: Reword the three field docs: lastPromptAt 'newest press a turn used (or the file recorded); null when none', consumedAt 'newest press used by a stopped or lost turn or read from the file', session 'null until session.start, session.attach or the first recorded stop'.

minor.name: 'ten TypeScript mods' pin duplicates test_mod_count and breaks on the next mod
minor.summary: test_claude_md_names_and_counts_the_mod asserts the literal phrase "ten TypeScript mods". tests/contract/test_mod_count.py already checks that CLAUDE.md's count word matches the number of mods in the marketplace. The literal copy adds no coverage, and when an eleventh mod lands, the lap-stamp test also fails, so that PR has to edit an unrelated mod's test.
fix: Drop the line asserting "ten TypeScript mods" (line 60) and leave the count to tests/contract/test_mod_count.py; keep the name and mirror-test assertions.
